title: Post-Course Portfolio: Notes Web App
descriptionMarkdown:
# Notes Web App

## Position in the curriculum
Post-course portfolio expansion: build after finishing the full curriculum through the final capstone. Pair this with the URL Shortener as a second simple Spring Boot project, this time focused on full CRUD (create, read, update, delete) on one entity plus a real frontend/backend integration boundary, rather than a single write-then-redirect flow.

## Already-proven foundation
The final capstone's own delivery sequence already required an HTTP adapter with DTOs, status/error semantics, and pagination. This project applies that exact sequence to a second, differently-shaped resource end to end, including serving a minimal browser-based frontend against it.

## Project scope
A `Note` entity (title, body, created/updated timestamps) behind full CRUD endpoints: `POST /api/notes`, `GET /api/notes` (paginated, with a query parameter for a text search over title/body), `GET /api/notes/{id}`, `PUT /api/notes/{id}` (full replace, idempotent per Chapter 18's semantics), `DELETE /api/notes/{id}`. Return `404` for an operation on a missing note, and `409` if a `PUT` includes a stale `updatedAt`/version field (optimistic locking, per Chapter 24). Serve a minimal static frontend (plain HTML/JS is sufficient; no framework required) from the same Spring Boot application that lists notes, lets a user create/edit/delete one, and displays validation errors returned by the API rather than a generic failure message.

## Required evidence
- Full CRUD integration tests (`@SpringBootTest` or `@WebMvcTest` plus `@DataJpaTest`) covering the happy path and every documented error status.
- A pagination test confirming page size and ordering are correct and stable across pages.
- An optimistic-locking test where a `PUT` using a stale version is rejected with `409`, not silently applied.
- Browser-based manual verification (a short screen recording or a written walkthrough) showing create, edit, delete, and a displayed validation error working end to end through the frontend.
- A `Dockerfile` building a non-root runtime image for the service, per Chapter 25's container discipline.

## Review and completion
A reviewer edits the same note in two open browser tabs, saves one, then tries to save the other, and expects a clear conflict message rather than one edit silently overwriting the other. They also disable JavaScript and confirm the API alone (via curl or an HTTP client) still enforces every validation and status-code rule the frontend was relying on.
learningObjectives: Implement full CRUD with correct HTTP status codes and idempotent PUT semantics
Add pagination and a text search parameter to a list endpoint
Apply optimistic locking to a REST update and surface the conflict clearly to a caller
Serve a minimal frontend from the same service and keep server-side validation authoritative regardless of client behavior
Package the finished service as a non-root container image
